stories.title: The first self-driving vehicle on Mars has proven to be a smashing success
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Perseverance rover has demonstrated significant autonomous capability on Mars.
Approximately 90% of the rover's travel has been self-driven.
This marks a major success in autonomous systems for extraterrestrial exploration.

stories.title: DeepMind’s hurricane breakthrough has surprised weather scientists
stories.author: Victoria Turk, wired.com
bullet_points: DeepMind has achieved a significant breakthrough in weather prediction using AI.
The open-source WeatherNext model demonstrates accuracy even with lower-resolution weather data.
The findings have surprised established weather scientists, indicating a potential shift in meteorological modeling.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times for LLMs.
The updated engine also enhances model output quality and reduces memory consumption.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents entirely on local, personal hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, now integrates MLX for enhanced performance.
This update specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing LLM execution on Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for local AI accessibility on macOS.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Judge rules Meta caused "public nuisance" and must fund mental health treatment
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A New Mexico judge ruled that Meta caused a 'public nuisance' related to youth mental health.
The ruling mandates that Meta fund a $567 million program to address the youth mental health crisis.
This case represents a significant legal action holding a major tech company accountable for platform impact.

stories.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
stories.author: Nuno Vasconcelos
bullet_points: Proposes a novel method for On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPD/OSPD) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses a key limitation of existing methods by achieving self-distillation without external supervision (ground-truth or external guidance).
The core innovation relies on leveraging the model's own generations via internal consistency.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon hardware.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: An Amazon data center could have the worst polluting power plant in the country
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Amazon is investing in a new power plant in West Texas to support a new data center.
The proposed gas-burning power plant could become one of the largest single sources of greenhouse gases in the US.
The development highlights the environmental impact associated with large-scale data center infrastructure.

stories.title: Europe's free satellite service just made it easier to track wildfires
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The Copernicus Browser has been updated to include wildfire visualization capabilities.
This enhancement is relevant to the ongoing record wildfire season in Europe.
It leverages Europe's free satellite service to improve wildfire tracking and monitoring.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark for evaluating selective trust in reasoning.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering better automation and evidence traceability.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluation methods by allowing for certified anytime-valid stopping.
Claims to achieve 74x cost reduction in agent evaluation while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Video Language Models (VLMs) struggle with precise event bookkeeping in real-world video data.
Current benchmarks are limited because they either lack control (real-world clips) or lack granular auditing (programmatic benchmarks).
The paper introduces 'trace-grounded parametric profiling' to accurately count events in controlled video tasks.

stories.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
stories.author: Jerzy Stefanowski
bullet_points: The paper addresses critical limitations in the evaluation of Explainable AI (XAI) methods.
It demonstrates challenges using the DetoxAI system for bias detection and concept unlearning in image recognition.
The research explores adapting explanation methods, such as counterfactuals, to handle concept drift in evolving data streams.

stories.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
stories.author: Juanzi Li
bullet_points: Introduces TRAJDEBUG, a method designed to trace the error lifecycle in long-horizon agent trajectories.
Addresses the critical challenge of debugging LLM-based agentic systems which suffer from cascading errors.
Focuses on identifying the earliest error step responsible for a final failure, despite evidence being scattered across long sequences.

stories.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
stories.author: Kristian J. Hammond
bullet_points: Introduces TYTAN, a system designed to automatically construct analytic semantic schemas from relational data.
Addresses the 'knowledge-acquisition bottleneck' where data understanding (entity types, measures, relationships) is currently done manually.
Aims to improve scalability and reduce dependency on domain experts for data analysis tools.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Introduces 'selective trust' as a new paradigm, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Presents MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test context reliability under various conditions.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: Addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, specifically for heart failure.
Proposes an 'Evidence-Linked Pipeline' to automate feature creation by integrating fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
Critiques existing methods (rule-based and LLM-based) for lacking full automation and maintainability.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional agent evaluation by providing a certified anytime-valid stopping mechanism.
Claims to reduce evaluation costs by 74x compared to existing methods while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
stories.author: Kai Jia
bullet_points: Introduces CalibForge, an autonomous system for synthesizing terminal tasks in AI training.
The system uses adversarial solver calibration to ensure tasks are appropriately challenging for learning, not just solvable.
Addresses the gap between task feasibility (executability) and task difficulty relative to a specific solver setting.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in applying generative reward models (GRMs) to Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core issue identified is the mismatch between GRMs' comparative nature and RL algorithms' scalar scoring paradigm.
The authors propose a method (RRC) to bridge this gap, aiming to unlock the potential of GRMs in LLM RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.), not just the model weights.
The paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a framework for evaluating automated harness optimization—the use of AI to iteratively improve the system surrounding an LLM.
A key gap identified is the lack of a common protocol within the community for measuring and standardizing harness optimization.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark to evaluate context-dependent reasoning.

stories.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
stories.author: Vamse Kumar Subbiah
bullet_points: The paper investigates programmatic tool calling (PTC) as an evolution of LLM tool use, allowing models to act beyond training data.
PTC replaces rigid JSON calls with executable scripts, enabling natural chaining and parallelization for code-capable models.
The research addresses a gap by empirically comparing PTC against native JSON tool calling on established benchmarks under real-world conditions.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluations by allowing stopping as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered.
Provides a certified guarantee that the evaluation's confidence level remains valid even with early stopping.

stories.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
stories.author: Shujian Huang
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of extending Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning capabilities across multiple languages.
It introduces RP-OPSD, a novel method that integrates 'Reasoning-Pivot-Guided' mechanisms into On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD).
The core contribution is explicitly prioritizing critical reasoning signals during distillation to improve cross-lingual transfer performance.

stories.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
stories.author: Abigail Goldsteen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of poor quality in existing benchmarks used to evaluate conversational AI agents.
It introduces a novel, reference-free framework utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) as judges to assess benchmark quality.
This framework provides actionable diagnostics regarding benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.

stories.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
stories.author: Tianyong Hao
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in evaluating LLMs for rule-intensive document review, a critical need in professional applications.
National standard documents (e.g., China GB/T) are proposed as a challenging and representative testbed due to their length and strict structural rules.
Current LLM benchmarks are criticized for focusing too much on domain knowledge and Q&A, neglecting intrinsic rule adherence.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in applying generative reward models (GRMs) to Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core issue identified is the mismatch between GRM's comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling the use of GRMs in RL.

stories.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
stories.author: Tabarakul Hazarika
bullet_points: The paper critiques the standard 'chunk-embed-top-k' approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over long documents.
It argues this standard design is structurally unsound, particularly for complex, structured documents like financial statements and audit reports.
The authors propose replacing black-box retrieval with more interpretable, agentic operations to handle data complexity (e.g., tables, near-identical figures).

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, orchestration, etc.), not just the model weights.
The paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, focusing on the critical need for automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system.
A major gap in the field is the lack of a common protocol or benchmark for evaluating and comparing these complex LLM harnesses.

stories.title: Human vs. AI – Diff-based line-level provenance for text under agentic editing
stories.author: eighttrigrams
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of tracking text provenance when AI agents perform edits.
It introduces a 'diff-based line-level provenance' method to maintain traceability.
This is relevant for ensuring accountability and understanding modifications made by autonomous AI systems.

stories.title: 🏦 Vaya: an AI loan advisor that asks whether you can still afford to live
stories.author: minhlong2605
bullet_points: Vaya is an AI loan advisor designed to shift focus from just lowest interest rates.
The tool emphasizes assessing a user's actual affordability to live, rather than just comparing rates.
It represents a move toward more holistic, personalized financial advice using AI in the lending sector.

stories.title: MCP Went Stateless: What the 2026-07-28 Spec Actually Changes
stories.author: krlz
bullet_points: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has been updated to become stateless, removing handshake and session management.
This change is highlighted as a significant development for agent infrastructure in the current year.
The article provides a practical, concise implementation example of a stateless server in Python.
